body:
Depends on #531.

### The problem

An arrow function without braces in the first branch of a ternary goes on
after the colon of the ternary, and takes the second branch:

```js
function choose(strict, b) {
  const eq = strict ? (x, y) => x === y : (x, y) => x == y || b;
  return eq;
}
```

```
$ lizard a.js          # master, 01afe9c
       1      2     16      0       1 (anonymous)@2-2@a.js
       4      2     22      2       4 choose@1-4@a.js
```

Only one arrow function is reported, with the `||` of the second one.

### What changes

`lizard_languages/javascript_functions.py` and
`lizard_languages/typescript_states.py`. The colon of a ternary that was
opened before an arrow function without braces now ends it; a ternary inside
its body, `x => x ? 1 : 2`, keeps its colon. With the fix:

```
       1      1      4      0       1 (anonymous)@2-2@a.js
       1      2      6      0       1 (anonymous)@2-2@a.js
       4      2     29      2       4 choose@1-4@a.js
```

### How it is tested

`Test_ES6_arrow_function_in_a_branch_of_a_ternary` in
`test/test_languages/testES6.py`, which fails without the change. The full
suite passes on the branch: `python -m pytest test` gives 1668 passed,
7 skipped. pycodestyle reports no new warnings in the changed files.

### What does not change

Ternaries inside the body of an arrow function, and ternaries outside arrow
functions.

Thanks for maintaining lizard and for taking the time to look at this.
title: End a JavaScript arrow function in a branch of a ternary at its colon
